    Statements of the pretorsion theorems #

    This file uses only Mathlib. It fixes the vocabulary of the manuscript Pretorsion theories and image-closed subcategories and states its principal results:

    • TheoremA (Theorem A = Theorem 4.4): for a subcategory Z of the category mod Λ of finite-dimensional right modules over a finite-dimensional algebra Λ, the following are equivalent: Z is image-closed; Z = Gen Z ∩ Cogen Z; Z = T ∩ F for a pretorsion theory (T, F).
    • CompleteLattice (Theorem 3.6): the pretorsion theories of mod Λ, ordered by (T, F) ≤ (T', F') iff T ⊆ T' and F ⊇ F', form a complete lattice, with the meet and join of a nonempty family given by (3.2) and (3.3) and with (0, mod Λ) and (mod Λ, 0) as least and greatest elements.
    • TheoremBPretorsion and TheoremBImageClosed (Theorem B = Theorems 7.5 and 8.5 at x = 1): for the linearly oriented quiver 1 → 2 → ⋯ → n, the pretorsion theories counted by the number of indecomposables in T ∩ F, and the image-closed subcategories counted by their number of indecomposables, are enumerated by Han and Zeng's q-Gandhi polynomials B_{n+1}(1, q) and C_{n+1}(1, q).
    • GandhiPretorsion and GandhiImageClosed (Theorems 7.5 and 8.5): the two-variable refinements, with x recording the number of indecomposables whose support ends at the last vertex.

    Conventions follow the manuscript. k is an arbitrary field and Λ a finite-dimensional k-algebra. Modules are finite-dimensional right modules, realized as finitely generated modules over Λᵐᵒᵖ. A subcategory is a property of objects closed under isomorphisms, finite direct sums and direct summands (Subcategory). Representations of 1 → 2 → ⋯ → n are functors from the linear order Fin n to finite-dimensional k-vector spaces; the manuscript identifies mod Λ_n with them. The number of indecomposable objects of a subcategory is the number of isomorphism classes of its indecomposable objects. Polynomials in q and x live in ℤ[q][x], written (ℤ[X])[X] with q the inner and x the outer variable. All types live in one universe u.

            def PretorsionImageClosed.Statement.IsPretorsionTheory {C : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} C] (T F : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty C) :

            (T, F) is a pretorsion theory (Definition 2.2): with Z = T ⊓ F, every morphism from T to F is Z-trivial, and every object X sits in a short Z-preexact sequence T' ⟶ X ⟶ F' with T' in T and F' in F.

              Type u_1

              A subcategory in the sense of the manuscript's conventions: a property of objects closed under isomorphisms and direct summands (retracts) and under finite direct sums (binary direct sums and the zero objects). Full subcategories are given by their objects.

              • prop : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty C

                The objects of the subcategory.

              • prop_of_retract {X Y : C} : ∀ (a : CategoryTheory.Retract X Y), self.prop Y → self.prop X

                Closed under direct summands, hence under isomorphisms.

              • prop_biprod {X Y : C} : self.prop X → self.prop Y → self.prop (X ⊞ Y)

                Closed under finite direct sums: under binary direct sums ...

              • prop_of_isZero {X : C} : CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero X → self.prop X

                ... and containing the zero objects (the empty direct sum).

                                            source
                                            def PretorsionImageClosed.Statement.IsDelta (f g : Polynomial Rq) :
                                            Prop

                                            g = Δ_q f in ℤ[q][x] (Definition 1.1, (1.2)): g · (1 + (q - 1) x) = f(1 + q x) - f(x). Since ℤ[q][x] is a domain and 1 + (q - 1) x ≠ 0, g is determined by f.
